Tutorial 01.04: More examples

This tutorial gives a list of simple examples to try out in the constructGraph() function.

00001 #ifndef _MAINCOMPONENT_H_
00002 #define _MAINCOMPONENT_H_
00003 
00004 #include <juce/juce.h>
00005 #include "../../UGen/UGen.h"
00006 
00007 class MainComponent : public Component,
00008 public JuceIOHost
00009 { 
00010 public:
00011   MainComponent () : JuceIOHost(0, 2) { } 
00012   
00013   UGen constructGraph(UGen const& input)
00014   {
00015     // replace the entire body of this function with the examples in the HTML tutorial
00016     return SinOsc::AR(1000, 0, 0.1);
00017   }
00018 };
00019 
00020 #endif //_MAINCOMPONENT_H_

Notice the JuceIOHost is set up for 2-in and 2-out.

You can copy and paste each of these examples to replace the entire body of the constructGraph() function. In fact you can use these examples to test the iPhone project too (use the iPhone_UGen_AU/UGenRemoteIO.xcodeproj). In this case the constructGraph() is an Objective-C function but works in a similar way to the Juce project.

Note that you can click on the name of a UGen (e.g., SinOsc) and it should to take you to its more detailed documentation.

Amplitude modulation: 

  UGen mod = SinOsc::AR(4, 0, 0.1, 0.2);
  UGen output = SinOsc::AR(1000, 0, mod);
  return output;

Frequency modulation: 

  UGen mod = SinOsc::AR(4, 0, 100, 1000);
  UGen output = SinOsc::AR(mod, 0, 0.3);
  return output;

Sawtooth: 

  UGen output = LFSaw::AR(200, 0, 0.3);
  return output;

Subtractive (low pass filter): 

  UGen saw = LFSaw::AR(200, 0, 0.3);
  UGen output = BLowPass::AR(saw, 400, 0.2); // 0.2 is a Q of 1/0.2 = 5
  return output;

Modulated filter: 

  UGen saw = LFSaw::AR(200, 0, 0.3);
  UGen mod = SinOsc::AR(4, 0, 100, 400);
  UGen output = BLowPass::AR(saw, mod, 0.2);
  return output;

Multichannel expansion (multichannel inputs force UGens lower down the chain to be multichannel too) as described in the earlier tutorial Tutorial 01.03: Building more complex UGen graphs: 

  UGen saw = LFSaw::AR(200, 0, 0.3);
  UGen modFreq = U(4.9, 5.1); // U() is handy a macro for multichannel constant "arrays"
  UGen mod = SinOsc::AR(modFreq, 0, 100, 400);
  UGen output = BLowPass::AR(saw, mod, 0.2);
  return output;

Mixing: you can use the standard arithmetic operator + to do this (you can also use the * operator to do multiplication with UGens and other aritmetic operators too). 

   UGen sine1 = SinOsc::AR(200, 0, 0.05);
   UGen sine2 = SinOsc::AR(555, 0, 0.05);
   UGen sine3 = SinOsc::AR(1000, 0, 0.05);
   UGen sine4 = SinOsc::AR(1234, 0, 0.05);
   UGen output = sine1 + sine2 + sine3 + sine4;
   return output;

More mixing (exactly the same result as the example above but more efficient especially with many channels): 

   UGen sines = SinOsc::AR(U(200, 555, 1000, 1234), 0, 0.05);
   UGen output = Mix::AR(sines);
   return output;

Yet more mixing (absolutely identical to the example above mix() is a convenience function): 

   UGen sines = SinOsc::AR(U(200, 555, 1000, 1234), 0, 0.05);
   UGen output = sines.mix();
   return output;

Grouping and mixing: 

   UGen sines = SinOsc::AR(U(200, 555, 1000, 1234), 0, 0.05);
   UGen output = sines.groupMix(2); // 200 & 1000 on left, 555 & 1234 on right
   return output;

Soundfile playback using a memory-based buffer. Here you may need to change the path to the soundfile. If you are testing this in the iPhone project the guitar.wav sample is included in the project and the iPhone UGen++ wrapper automatically searches for soundfiles in the application bundle (if the path is NOT already a full path). On the Juce (Mac/Windows) projects you will need to specify the full path to any AIFF or WAV file (16 or 24 bits). E.g., "/Users/JoeBloggs/Desktop/guitar.wav" or "~/Desktop/guitar.wav" on the Mac, or "C:\\Documents and Settings\\JoeBloggs\\Desktop\\guitar.wav" on Windows (notice the double backslashes required in code on Windows). 

  Buffer sound("guitar.wav");
  float rate = 1.0;
  float trigger = 0.0;
  float startPos = 0.0;
  float loop = 1.0;
  UGen output = PlayBuf::AR(sound, rate, trigger, startPos, loop);
  return output;

Same as above but using a rate of 0.0 and deriving your own "phasor" (a rising sawtooth signal) to drive the "playback head" using the startPos input. The rate needs to be the reciprocal of the duration of the buffer (so a 2 second buffer would need a rate of 0.5Hz to play back at its normal speed) and the phasor needs to run from zero to the index of the last sample (i.e., one less than the buffer size). Here we use LinLin to map a linear range onto another linear range. 

   Buffer sound("guitar.wav");
   float rate = 0.0;
   float trigger = 0.0;
   UGen startPos = LFSaw::AR(1.0/sound.duration(), 0, 1);
   startPos = LinLin::AR(startPos, -1, 1, 0, sound.size()-1);
   float loop = 1.0;
   UGen output = PlayBuf::AR(sound, rate, trigger, startPos, loop);
   return output;

Simple delay (all the delay UGens require a maximum delay time to be specified in order to allocate any internal buffers): 

  Buffer sound("guitar.wav");
  float rate = 1.0;
  float trigger = 0.0;
  float startPos = 0.0;
  float loop = 1.0;
  UGen playbuf = PlayBuf::AR(sound, rate, trigger, startPos, loop); 
  
  const float maximumDelay = 2.0;
  UGen output = DelayL::AR(playbuf, maximumDelay, U(0.0, 0.5));
  
  return output;

Modulated delay: 

  Buffer sound("guitar.wav");
  float rate = 1.0;
  float trigger = 0.0;
  float startPos = 0.0;
  float loop = 1.0;
  UGen playbuf = PlayBuf::AR(sound, rate, trigger, startPos, loop);
  
  const float maximumDelay = 2.0;
  UGen delayTime = SinOsc::AR(U(2.9, 3.1), 0, 0.001, 0.002);
  UGen output = DelayL::AR(playbuf, maximumDelay, delayTime);
 
  return output;

Rericulating/feedback delay (feedback amount is specified as a time in seconds for the recirculated signal to decay by 60dBs): 

  Buffer sound("guitar.wav");
  float rate = 1.0;
  float trigger = 0.0;
  float startPos = 0.0;
  float loop = 1.0;
  UGen playbuf = PlayBuf::AR(sound, rate, trigger, startPos, loop);
 
  const float maximumDelay = 2.0;
  float decayTime = 3.0;
  UGen output = CombL::AR(playbuf, maximumDelay, U(0.49, 0.51), decayTime);
 
  return output;

Audio input: an audio input (AudioIn) UGen is passed in as the argument to constructGraph() function. This should have an appropriate number of channels as set by the host (you can use the getNumChannels() function to find out).

e.g., simple (0.5s) delay: 

   UGen output = DelayL::AR(input, 0.5, 0.5);
   return output;

White noise: 

  UGen output = WhiteNoise::AR(0.1);
  return output;

Random modulation, and using linear to exponential mapping: 

  UGen noise = WhiteNoise::AR(0.1);
  UGen mod = LFNoise2::AR(2); // -1...+1
  mod = LinExp::AR(mod, -1, 1, 200, 10000); // linear to exponential: 200...10000
  UGen output = BLowPass::AR(noise, mod, 0.2);
  return output;

Panning: 

  UGen mod = SinOsc::AR(0.5, 0, 1);   // pan position -1...+1
  UGen mono = SinOsc::AR(1000, 0, 0.2);
  UGen output = Pan2::AR(mono, mod);    // constant power pan
  return output;
